skill_entry.name: 14. Disabled code left in the tree (`#if 0` blocks and commented-out statements)
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, all mechanical. (a) The diff adds `#if 0` or `#if false` (a preprocessor block no build compiles). (b) A touched h/ or src/ file holds an unchanged `#if 0` block at HEAD within 20 lines of a hunk start (PR 2148 h/pos/hwattention.hpp:507 sits outside both hunks of the file). (c) In h/ or src/ the diff adds a `//` line that is a statement: it starts with `if (`, `for (`, `while (`, `}` or an identifier followed by `(` or ` = `, ends with `;`, `{`, `(` or `,`, is not a log, dump or exit call, and holds no run of four lowercase words. (d) A removed line reappears in the same file with `//` in front and passes the statement test of (c) (PR 1997 `if (pdc + 1 == dev->num_fetchers) {`).
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Run the step 1-3 commands of procedures.md: added disabled lines mapped to HEAD lines, removed lines that reappear commented in the same file, unchanged `#if 0` blocks within 20 lines of a hunk. 2. Per `#if 0` block: read to `#endif`, record line count and kind (debug prints, disabled production logic, disabled test code), and test the first statement inside against `git show BASE:FILE`: present verbatim means live code switched off (PR 2461 src/pos/worker.cpp:769). 3. Per commented statement: find a live call or assignment of the same name in the same function (PR 1920 hwattention.hpp:655 next to the live wait at :649) or a commented declaration in another file (device.hpp:338-339 for device.cpp:90-91). 4. Read the two lines above for a stated reason; a PR-body sentence is not one (PR 2461 body says 'behind `#if 0`', Wade asked anyway). 5. Report once per file: first hit is the finding, later hits are 'same at'.
skill_entry.question: Does any build compile this text, and if not, why is it in the tree instead of deleted, or is it a reference the author means to keep (then a one-line comment should say so)?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A disabled line or block whose two preceding lines say why it is off or where the behavior moved (PR 2008 h/pos/hwattention.hpp:816, :847 under 'performing our wait one layer down inside the xfer function', approved with no text); a line that only says what the code would do is no reason (PR 1920 :654). Commented-out log, dump or exit calls (PR 1920 head: 15 `// spdlog::` lines, `// debug_exit` at :507). Commented statements under t/ (PR 1666 :1371-1374, :1423; PR 1920 t_hwattention.cpp:170). An old signature above a definition (PR 1920 :443-444). `#ifdef NAME` blocks (debug-switch-or-output-left-on). A single commented-out wait, sleep, lock, assert or check live at BASE (silent-behavior-change owns it, 3307473806). A block the author told a human reviewer is kept on purpose (PR 2461 3102946251): never repeat, never block.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (A) commented statement: "`<file>:<line>` is a commented-out <guard | call | assignment> that nothing compiles; the live `<call>` at :<line> already does the work. can this go away? Or are you leaving it as reference for an alternative strategy (then a one-line comment should say so)?" (B) `#if 0` block: "`<file>:<line>` is an `#if 0` block of N lines (<debug prints | a <check | wait> that was live at BASE and is now silent>) that nothing compiles. if this isn't useful, should get rid of it. <same at :<line>, :<line>>"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: No severity word in any of the seven texts. Question form in four (2737935271, 2915191812, 2620242347, 2737826254: 'can this go away?', 'can we get rid of this dead code?'), statement in two (2771711406 'can probably just remove the commented lines', 3102601258 'if this isn't useful, should get rid of it'), one echo (3102603313 'same here'). He approved with the code still in (PR 1920 :655 at 2d53016b44; PR 2461 both blocks at 9d0d649274, three minutes after the asks). The check is a 6-of-8 signal on the hwattention_sync branch: PRs 1666, 1920, 1997, 2148, 2461, 2766 drew a comment; PR 2008 (commented waits with a reason above) and PR 2135 (a new 15-line `#if 0` at h/pos/hwattention.hpp:764 plus the unchanged spdlog block at :492, the block he asked about eight days later in PR 2148) were approved with no text. Treat as minor, not blocking, one nit per file; never escalate.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (2915191812 has an empty diff_hunk and original_line 507, a line outside every hunk); the BASE file (first-statement test); another file (h/pos/device.hpp for the declarations behind device.cpp:90-91); PR review comments, for an author reply to a human reviewer. Not PR body, commits, CI or runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: disabled code left in the tree

BASE for this check: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha` when online. Offline, or when `origin/<base_ref>` is absent from WT (PR 2461: no `origin/wm-bill-hwsync1`): BASE = the second parent of the newest merge on HEAD's first-parent line, `git -C WT log --first-parent --merges -1 --format=%P HEAD | cut -d" " -f2` (PR 2461: b539439a18, same as base.sha). If there is no merge, ask for base.sha. Never use origin/main for a PR against a feature branch (PR 2461: 5f37572171, a huge diff).

1. Added lines that are `#if 0`/`#if false` or commented-out statements, with HEAD file:line. The awk counts every added line, blank ones included (a bare `+` must advance the counter, or every later number in the hunk is low by one per blank line: the earlier awk printed PR 1920 :451 for the block at :458). The greps keep code syntax, drop prose (a run of four lowercase words), drop log, dump and exit calls with any namespace prefix (`//tron::hardware::debug_exit(...)`, PR 2461 worker.cpp:775), and keep only `#if 0` lines under t/:
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3); next} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]-1; next} /^\+/{n++; print f":"n":"substr($0,2)}' \
| grep -E ':[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*if[[:space:]]+(0|false)[[:space:]]*$|:[[:space:]]*//[[:space:]]*(if \(|for \(|while \(|else|\}|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:.>-]*(\(|[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]).*[;{(,]$)' \
| grep -v -E '//[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*::)*(spdlog::|debug_hexdump|debug_bf16dump|debug_exit|dbg_)' \
| grep -v -E '//[^;{(,]*([a-z]+ ){3,}[a-z]+' \
| grep -v -E '^t/[^:]*:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*//' > disabled.txt
```
2. Removed lines that reappear commented in the same file, passing the statement test and the log-call exclusion of step 1 (a removed log, dump or exit call that comes back commented is not a hit; a removed wait, sleep, lock, assert, warn or check that comes back commented goes to silent-behavior-change, not here):
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} /^\+[ \t]*\/\//{l=$0; sub(/^\+[ \t]*\/\/[ \t]*/,"",l); print f"\t"l}' \
| while IFS=$'\t' read -r f l; do git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- "${f#a/}" | grep -E '^-[^-]' | sed -E 's/^-[ \t]*//' | grep -qxF -- "$l" \
  && echo "$l" | grep -qE '^(if \(|for \(|while \(|else|\}|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:.>-]*(\(|[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]))' \
  && echo "$l" | grep -qvE '^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*::)*(spdlog::|debug_hexdump|debug_bf16dump|debug_exit|dbg_)' \
  && echo "REAPPEARS in ${f#a/}: $l"; done
```
3. Unchanged `#if 0` blocks within 20 lines of a hunk start in touched h/ and src/ files, minus the step 1 hits (one command; `prfiles.txt` from the common setup):
```
for f in $(grep -E '^(h|src)/' prfiles.txt); do starts=$(git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- $f | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+).*/\1/' | tr '\n' ' '); git -C WT show HEAD:$f | grep -n -E '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*if[[:space:]]+(0|false)' | cut -d: -f1 | awk -v s="$starts" -v f=$f 'BEGIN{n=split(s,h," ")} {for(i=1;i<=n;i++) if ($1-h[i]<=20 && h[i]-$1<=20){print f":"$1; break}}'; done | grep -v -x -F -f <(cut -d: -f1,2 disabled.txt)
```
   Expect one or two unchanged debug blocks per worker-style file that Wade would not mention (PR 2148 src/pos/worker.cpp:1251, PR 1920 src/pos/worker.cpp:1154); they go into the per-file sentence after the first hit and never lead when a step 1 hit exists in the same file.
4. Per `#if 0` block: extent, kind, and whether it switches off code that was live at BASE. Take the first line inside the block that is not blank, a brace or a `//` comment; if it exists verbatim at BASE the block disables live code, else the block is new:
```
git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v s=LINE 'NR>=s{print NR": "$0} NR>s && /^[[:space:]]*#endif/{exit}'
first=$(git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v s=LINE 'NR>s && /^[[:space:]]*#endif/{exit} NR>s && !/^[[:space:]]*([{}]|\/\/.*)?[[:space:]]*$/{print; exit}'); git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -qxF -- "$first" && echo LIVE-AT-BASE || echo NEW
```
5. Per commented statement: live twin in the same function, and a commented declaration elsewhere (residue pair):
```
git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'NAME'                      # live call or assignment of the same name
git -C WT grep -n -E '//[[:space:]]*(size_t|int|bool|auto)?[[:space:]]*NAME' HEAD -- h src
```
6. Stated reason and author reply. The two lines above the block clear it when they say why it is off or where the behavior moved (PR 2008 :814-815); a comment naming the switch the block stands for (`// #ifdef DEBUG_RX_DESC`, PR 2148 worker.cpp:300) is a hypothesis-grade clear, reported in the per-file sentence only. A reply clears a block only when it answers a human reviewer (not a bot) and says the block is kept on purpose; a reply that says the disabled check is no longer valid (PR 2461 3101971874, to cursor[bot]) is a reason to delete, and Wade asked at :769 after it:
```
git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v s=LINE 'NR>=s-2 && NR<s{print NR": "$0}'
gh api --paginate repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --jq '.[] | select(.path=="FILE") | [.id,.user.login,.created_at,.in_reply_to_id,.original_line,(.body|.[0:120])] | @tsv'
```
7. Report once per file: first hit as the finding (shape A for a commented statement, shape B for an `#if 0` block), later hits as "same at :L, :L". A block that switches off a BASE-live check or wait gets the clause "now silent" in shape B and is not repeated by silent-behavior-change.

On PR 1997 (BASE ae5f6faec0, comment commit d306b805ce): step 1 hits h/pos/hwattention.hpp:703 `// if (pdc + 1 == dev->num_fetchers) {` and :706 `//}`; step 2 shows both reappear from removed lines of the same file; the live `wait_for_hbm_vwrite_complete(...)` at :704-705 is the call the guard used to wrap; the unchanged two-line `// wait_for_hbm_vwrite_complete(fpga_index, v_hwblock, ...` at :710-711 under the prose line :709 is not an added line and is reached only by step 1 of PR 1920 (:655); the two lines above :703 are code, no reason. Wade: 'can probably just remove the commented lines' (2771711406). At the approved head c502e4d61a the lines are gone and :703-704 carry the prose reason ('wait after every transfer for now ... chip hang'). On PR 2461 (BASE b539439a18, HEAD 9d0d649274) step 1 hits h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:468, src/pos/worker.cpp:769 and :797 (worker.cpp:775 `//tron::hardware::debug_exit(...)` is dropped by the exclusion); step 2 prints nothing; step 4 marks :769 LIVE-AT-BASE (`if (workreq->tok_ix < hardware::MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN) {`), :468 and :797 NEW. Wade commented on the first two (3102601258, 3102603313 'same here'). On PR 2148 (BASE e2ce886cca, HEAD 4491ff73db) step 1 hits only src/pos/worker.cpp:301; step 3 adds h/pos/hwattention.hpp:507 (hunk at :520, 4 lines after its `#endif`, -U0 headers `@@ -466 +466,6` and `@@ -514,0 +520,5`) and src/pos/worker.cpp:1251; Wade asked at :507 (2915191812). On PR 1920 (BASE a85c91e3f5 = second parent of the last merge, HEAD 620d1e83ba) step 1 hits hwattention.hpp:458, :655, model.hpp:1355, device.cpp:90-91, t_hwattention_replay.cpp:712; Wade asked at :656 (2737935271) and device.cpp:91 (2737826254). On PR 1666 (141b45251e..b0e53be7e0) step 1 hits t/t_hwattention.cpp:1379 (2620242347 anchors at :1380). On PR 2008 (d9d3f59155..3bf6517ac8, silent) step 1 hits hwattention.hpp:816 and :847, both cleared by the reason at :814-815 and :845-846. On PR 4557 (e5fa372c19..96a6220ab6, negative control) steps 1-3 print nothing.
final.widen_delta: New check, no existing check changes. Placement: after check 13 in "Checks on scope, history and ownership" as check 14; the description line of SKILL.md gains "disabled code left in the tree". One setup addition in procedures.md: the common-setup BASE line gets the feature-branch rule (base.sha, or offline the second parent of the newest first-parent merge; never origin/main for a PR against a feature branch), because the SKILL.md Words entry defines BASE as `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` and that gives a wrong BASE for the five member PRs. Cross-references, written in the new entry only: (1) a single commented-out wait, sleep, lock, assert or check that was live at BASE is owned by silent-behavior-change-or-unexamined-threshold (3307473806) and is not reported here; an `#if 0` block that switches off such a line is reported here with the "now silent" clause (3102603313) and silent-behavior-change does not repeat it; (2) a `#ifdef NAME` block with a named macro belongs to debug-switch-or-output-left-on; (3) a commented-out declaration pair (device.hpp:338-339 with device.cpp:90-91) overlaps dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition and is written once, here. Check 10 keeps its hunk-to-claim trace: disabled text never carries a PR identifier and never reaches check 10's candidate test.
